decks.name: LeetCode #238 - Product of Array Except Self
decks.description: Return an array where each element is the product of all other elements except itself

cards.question: Product of Array Except Self: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i]. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.

solutions.name: Prefix and Suffix Optimal
solutions.explanation: Use the output array to store prefix products in first pass, then multiply by suffix products in reverse pass. This achieves O(n) time with O(1) extra space by reusing the output array. Most space-efficient solution.

mentalModel.keyInsight: Two passes: prefix from left captures everything before me, suffix from right captures everything after me.
mentalModel.whyItWorks: Each position needs the product of all elements except itself. By multiplying the prefix product (everything to the left) by the suffix product (everything to the right), we get exactly that — without ever including the element itself.

commonMistakes.why: Starting at zero makes every product zero. The multiplicative identity is 1.
Store prefix BEFORE multiplying by current element — the current element must be excluded from its own result.

commonMistakes.wrong: res[i] = postfix  // assignment in second pass
commonMistakes.right: res[i] *= postfix  // multiply in second pass
commonMistakes.why: Second pass must MULTIPLY into the existing prefix value, not overwrite it. Overwriting loses the prefix products.

solutions.name: Prefix and Suffix Arrays
solutions.explanation: Create separate arrays for prefix and suffix products. The result at each index is the product of its prefix and suffix values. Clear approach but uses extra O(n) space for the prefix and suffix arrays.

trace: Build pref → pref[1]=nums[0]*pref[0]=1*1=1, pref[2]=nums[1]*pref[1]=2*1=2, pref[3]=nums[2]*pref[2]=3*2=6 → pref=[1,1,2,6]
Build suff → suff[2]=nums[3]*suff[3]=4*1=4, suff[1]=nums[2]*suff[2]=3*4=12, suff[0]=nums[1]*suff[1]=2*12=24 → suff=[24,12,4,1]

mentalModel.keyInsight: Split into 'everything before me' (prefix array) and 'everything after me' (suffix array), then multiply them together.
mentalModel.whyItWorks: pref[i] holds the product of all elements to the left of i, suff[i] holds the product of all elements to the right. Their product at each index gives the product of everything except nums[i].

commonMistakes.why: Base case must be 1 (nothing to the left of index 0). Using nums[0] would include the element itself.
pref[i] should be the product of elements BEFORE index i, so multiply nums[i-1] (not nums[i]) by the previous prefix.
suff[i] should be the product of elements AFTER index i, so multiply nums[i+1] (not nums[i]) by the next suffix.

semanticLines: Define function productExceptSelf(nums).
Get length of nums and store as n.
Create prefix array of n zeros.
Create suffix array of n zeros.
Set pref[0] to one — nothing to the left of first element.
Set suff[n-1] to one — nothing to the right of last element.
Build prefix products: each position stores product of all elements before it.
pref[i] = product of nums[0..i-1].
Build suffix products: each position stores product of all elements after it.
suff[i] = product of nums[i+1..n-1].
Combine: multiply prefix and suffix at each index to get result.
Return the result array.
codeLines: res = [pref[i] * suff[i] for i in range(n)]

solutions.name: Division
solutions.explanation: Calculate the total product of all non-zero elements, then divide by each element to get the result. Handle zero cases specially: if more than one zero exists, all results are zero; if exactly one zero, only that position gets the product. Not allowed in problem constraints but shown for understanding.

trace: zeroCount==1 → only zero position gets product: res[0]=0, res[1]=12, res[2]=0, res[3]=0

mentalModel.keyInsight: Total product ÷ self = everything else. Handle zeros as special cases.
mentalModel.whyItWorks: If no zeros: dividing total product by each element gives the product of all others. One zero: only the zero position gets a non-zero result (since all others include zero in their product). Two+ zeros: every position includes at least one zero, so everything is zero.

commonMistakes.wrong: for num in nums: prod *= num  // including zeros
commonMistakes.why: Including zeros in the total product makes it zero, losing all useful information.

commonMistakes.right: if zeroCount > 0: res[i] = prod if num == 0 else 0
commonMistakes.why: With one zero, only the zero position gets the product; all others must be zero since their product includes the zero element.

commonMistakes.right: res[i] = prod // num  // integer division in Python
commonMistakes.why: Use integer division to keep results as integers. Regular division produces floats.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: For each position, calculate the product of all other elements using nested loops. Skip the current index when multiplying. Least efficient but most straightforward approach.

trace: i=0: prod=1, skip j=0, prod*=2, prod*=3, prod*=4 → res[0]=24
i=1: prod=1, prod*=1, skip j=1, prod*=3, prod*=4 → res[1]=12
i=2: prod=1, prod*=1, prod*=2, skip j=2, prod*=4 → res[2]=8
i=3: prod=1, prod*=1, prod*=2, prod*=3, skip j=3 → res[3]=6

mentalModel.keyInsight: For each element, multiply everything else by skipping self.
mentalModel.whyItWorks: The most literal interpretation: for every position, loop through all other positions and multiply them together. Correct but slow at O(n²).

commonMistakes.wrong: prod *= nums[j]  // without skipping when i == j
commonMistakes.why: Without skipping, you include the element itself in its own product.
Multiplying by zero makes everything zero. The multiplicative identity is 1.
